title: Transcribe fixture: Fireball
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §10 fixture A Fireball card with a circle zone; DESIGN.md §4.1 (containment, templates), §4.3 (zones).

One scenario under packages/fixtures/scenarios/, in the format owned by the fixture scenario format bead. The format may not be changed by this bead; a gap blocks this bead and is reported against the format bead. Cover: template card owning its zone; spawn into a binder binding the new card and its new zone, asserting the card's zone reference was remapped to the new zone; dragging the zone onto the board removes it from the card's contents; creatures placed inside and outside the circle; Lock targets spawning one save_row per creature inside with target and owner set; scripted saves with one pass and one fail; Apply all adding damage_dealt per row; the Apply all log group (addressed by index) holds the resolved writes; a later change to a target dex_save drifts the live damage_dealt while that earlier log group is asserted unchanged; save rows are addressed through bind steps since they are created inside an action; Discard removing zone, card, and rows recursively.

Done when: the scenario passes the discovery test; a new test/titles-fireball.test.ts (owned by this bead) asserts the title; the docs/FIXTURES.md section links the file; pnpm lint and format:check pass.

Out of scope: other fixtures; evaluation; any change to the format.
notes: Codex review: one in-scope finding, fixed before merge (e49b2cc): if() returns its chosen branch unchanged, so a failed save's damage_dealt is the stored roll result, not a number; FIXTURES §9 drift example amended. Agent notes for M2: spawn owned-remap, spawn inside each appending to this in order, strict-inequality circle membership, container empty after move to board, is_zone readable on copies, add logs resulting sum, recursive remove. M1: roll result acts as total inside floor() and comparisons. Frozen variant (set at lock time) not transcribed.

Required variants: die with modifier as a formula following owner.attack_bonus, as a loose GM die with empty modifier, and owned by a goblin; goblin HIT visible to a player while ac is hidden; tray as a zone and as a cup container; re-hiding covers object visibility and opaque-zone behaviour, and a manual visible_to write creating an override that stops the formula. title: Fixture scenario format
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §10 (notation and intent), §2 (values), §3.1 (structural cells), §8 (actions, whole section), DESIGN.md §4.1 (objects, containment), §4.4 (visibility), §7 (operations, undo).

Design the machine-readable form of the §10 fixtures in packages/fixtures. Deliver TypeScript types, a zod validator, docs/FIXTURES.md, and tests. This bead owns the format; transcription beads may not change it. A scenario must be able to express everything below.

Table setup. Objects with unique id, tags, cells, and ordered `contents` (owning, acyclic). `container` is derived from contents, never written. An object is either in a container or placed on a board (board id, position, and shape for zones and tokens), never both. Non-owning references are a tagged value. Templates are objects marked as templates; instances are made from them by a spawn step. Per-cell visibility as in DESIGN §4.4.

Cell values. Every §2 storable value has an unambiguous tagged encoding: number, text, boolean, empty, reference, dice expression, roll result (with its parts), viewer set, ink. Formula source is a separate tagged form from literal text. Errors are expectations, never setup values.

Dice script. An ordered list of roll results consumed in order during execution. Exhaustion is a scenario error. The script is execution input only; it is not a replay mechanism (DESIGN §7 replays recorded effects). Shuffle takes an explicit permutation from the script.

Actions on an object: name, optional `when` source, ordered steps as source text. Steps performed by an actor (GM or a named viewer): set literal, override a formula cell, clear override, invoke action, move object to board position, move object into a container at an index, spawn template into a container or onto a board with initial cells and a symbolic binding for the new object (and for objects it owns), undo last action group.

Expectations after any step: cell value, cell error code, cell has override marker, action enabled or disabled, action invocation rejected with a reason and no state change, object exists or has been removed (recursively), object container and index, object board placement, ordered contents of an object, cell visible or hidden to a named viewer, object visible or hidden to a named viewer, number of log groups, and that the latest log group's resolved effects include a given cell write or roll.

Deliverables: src/types.ts, src/schema.ts (zod), src/index.ts exporting them plus loadScenario(path), test/format.test.ts with malformed examples the validator rejects, test/samples/ with two test-only sample scenarios (hit points, die with modifier) that the cells transcription bead later replaces with production scenarios under scenarios/. A test/scenarios.test.ts that discovers every file under scenarios/ and validates it; it passes trivially now. docs/FIXTURES.md with the format walkthrough and one stub section per §10 fixture, each with a link slot the transcription beads fill in.

Done when: docs/FIXTURES.md walks through every §10 fixture and shows how the format expresses each behaviour the prose calls out, with no unexpressible construct remaining; validator and sample tests pass; pnpm typecheck, lint, format:check pass.

Out of scope: transcribing the remaining fixtures; any evaluator, parser, or runner; replay expectations (M2 extends the format additively); face layout and show-when (M5 extends the format additively); depending on the schema package.

title: Workflow scripts: worktree, bead review, plan review
description:
Implements: CLAUDE.md Loop per implementation bead and Tracking: beads.

Add scripts/ (bash, no build step) that encode the loop:
- scripts/worktree.sh <bead-id> <slug>: creates branch <bead-id>/<slug> from main in ../vtt-worktrees/<bead-id>, runs pnpm install --frozen-lockfile there, and verifies bd works from inside the worktree with bd show <bead-id> (bd 1.3.4 already finds the main repo's .beads from a worktree; the script only needs to check, and fail loudly if it does not).
- scripts/review-bead.sh <bead-id> [base=main]: builds a review prompt from bd show <bead-id> plus a reminder that findings are advisory and must each be tagged IN-SCOPE or OUT-OF-SCOPE and that the review must state whether every Done-when condition is met, appends git diff <base>...HEAD excluding pnpm-lock.yaml in a fenced block, and runs `codex exec --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check -o <outfile> -` with that prompt on stdin from the current worktree. Do NOT use `codex review`: it rejects a custom prompt together with --base. Prints the review to stdout and saves it under .reviews/<bead-id>-<timestamp>.md (already gitignored).
- scripts/review-plan.sh <epic-id>: dumps the epic and each child via bd show, with a prompt asking for missing dependencies, overlapping scope, oversized beads, gaps against named doc sections, and bad decisions, each finding with bead id, severity (blocker / should-fix / nit), problem, and proposed change, ending with an overall verdict. Runs codex exec as above. Saves output like above.
Each script has a usage line, uses set -euo pipefail, and fails loudly on missing tools (bd, codex, pnpm, git). Scripts touch only scripts/ and a Workflow section appended to README.md.

Done when: each script runs end to end against a throwaway bead (create one with bd create, delete it with bd delete afterwards) in a throwaway worktree that is removed afterwards; pnpm lint and format:check pass; the README documents the three commands.

Out of scope: CI, automated merging, bead closing, anything that edits beads other than the throwaway.
close_reason: Merged to main in d83879e. Codex review: one in-scope finding (child enumeration by id prefix) fixed before merge.

title: Workspace root: pnpm, TypeScript, Vitest, Biome
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 (Platform), CLAUDE.md Stack.

Create the monorepo root with no packages yet, and settle the conventions every package bead follows.
- pnpm-workspace.yaml listing packages/*; root package.json (private, type module, packageManager pnpm 10, engines Node 26) with scripts: test (vitest run --passWithNoTests, see below), typecheck (pnpm -r --parallel typecheck), lint (biome check .), format (biome format --write .), format:check (biome format .).
- tsconfig.base.json: strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, isolatedModules, module ESNext, moduleResolution Bundler, target ES2023, noEmit. No composite, no project references. Each package will have tsconfig.json extending it and a typecheck script running tsc --noEmit. Libraries are consumed as TypeScript source: each package's exports map "." to ./src/index.ts, and Vite, Vitest, and tsx resolve that directly. No build step for libraries in v1.
- No root vitest.config.ts yet: Vitest errors when a projects glob matches nothing, so the library skeletons bead adds the root config with projects: ["packages/*"] when the first packages exist. Until then the root test script is `vitest run --passWithNoTests`; the skeletons bead drops the flag. Each package will own a vitest.config.ts.
- Biome as the single linter and formatter: biome.json at root with recommended rules, noUnusedVariables as an error, organize imports, 2-space indent, double quotes, line width 100. Markdown formatting off (the design docs are not reformatted); tool-managed folders (.beads, .agents, .claude, .codex, .cursor) excluded; ignoreUnknown on.
- .nvmrc / .node-version at the installed major (Node 26). .editorconfig. README.md with two lines pointing at docs/ and CLAUDE.md. Extend .gitignore with .reviews/.
- Add a Conventions subsection to CLAUDE.md: run pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm format:check, pnpm test before asking for review; libraries are source-consumed; one vitest.config.ts per package.

Done when: fresh clone, pnpm install, pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm format:check, pnpm test all exit 0 with zero packages present; introducing an unused variable in a scratch .ts file makes pnpm lint fail.

Out of scope: any package under packages/, CI, scripts/.
